newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs flatten as EMU, FX worries persist.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs flatten as EMU, FX worries persist.

text.p: Continued pressure on money market rates flattened the Belgian linear bond curve further on Thursday.

While the long-end of the curve remained supported by a set of benign economic data out of the U.S., dealers saw little chance for steepening trades to resume until worries over France's ability to meet the criteria for EMU and talk of a German rate hike went away.
"There's some nervousness in the market, especially in two-years and shorter," one trader said.

The front end of the OLO curve was following the money market, where rates remained under pressure as talk about the Bundesbank moving to a variable rate repo next week took hold. The expected publication on Monday, when the Belgian market is closed, of France's public finance audit was also weighing.

One-week repos crept up to 3.70/78 percent by late trade from 3.62/72 on Wednesday evening. However, the Belgian franc ended the day off its lows at 20.6475/85 to the mark, having played with 20.6500/10 midsession. One Luxembourg forex trader said there was no real interest in the mark crosses, including Belgium, with the focus on dollar/mark and mark/sterling.
At the long-end the two-to-five year area of the OLO curve flattened by three basis points to 95 basis points. The five-to-ten year area flattened by a little more than one basis point to 100 bps.

However, spreads over Germany remained fairly steady, one trader said. In the 10-year benchmark the spread widened by less than one basis point to eight to nine basis points, while in five-years the spread moved a bit more to minus one and a half basis points, he said.
